title: An inactive shop term still held by a customer blocks Delete
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure COD is the shop's default for new customers.
  • Make sure the shop has its own term A (made for this test), due on day 10 of the following month, deactivated and still held by one customer.
  • Start on the Credit Terms page (Settings, then "Credit Terms" in the Finance group), Active tab.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the "Inactive" tab.
  2. Click the "⋯" at the right of the term A row.
  3. Hover "Delete Credit Term".
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Inactive tab shows the term.

Step 2:

  • The menu shows exactly these items, in this order: "Reactivate" (rotate), "Move Customers" (person), "Delete Credit Term" (trash, in red, below a divider, greyed out).
  • Nothing else shows.

Step 3:

  • The hover reads "Used by 1 customer" with "Deactivate it instead to take it out of the pickers." below it.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11671 (Story 2, Row menu actions), story SV-11672 (Story 3, Create or edit a credit term), story SV-11673 (Story 4, Move Customers)

  • S2-R1: “Each row's "⋯" menu shows only the items that apply to that term, in this order. An item that applies but is blocked shows greyed out and does nothing when clicked; hovering it shows the reason.”
  • S2-R10: “Make Default is not available on inactive terms (it is absent from their menu).”
  • S4-N3: “Inactive terms and Credit Hold are valid sources (Move Customers is how a shop empties a deactivated term). Inactive terms are never offered in "Move To".”
  • S3-N2: “If the term is in use, standard, or inactive, Edit is not offered or is blocked (Story 2: Row menu actions), so the window cannot open in Edit mode for it.”
